text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This original research paper explicitly focuses on spatially explicit land use change (LUC) prediction in Brazil at a national scale, disaggregated into six macro-regions. The primary objective is to spatiotemporally assess LUC dynamics resulting from increased biofuel (ethanol) demand, including implementation of multiple future scenarios with quantitative comparison of land use changes and related greenhouse gas emissions. The study uses an integrated modeling framework combining a global CGE model (MAGNET), a spatial land use allocation model (PLUC), and a GIS-based carbon module, producing mapped LUC projections and quantitative metrics of change. The paper meets all core inclusion criteria (explicit national-scale spatial implementation, LUC prediction as central research question, multiple quantitative future scenarios, spatial modeling with quantitative outputs) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Although linked to bioenergy, the focus is on LUC prediction and mitigation at the national scale, not solely on biomass or carbon modeling. Therefore, it qualifies as an 'OK' paper under the criteria.
